items.title: Govt limits public disclosure of bureaucrats’ assets
items.description: • Selected asset information of BS-17, above officers to be made public • Government cites security concerns for withholding full asset declarations ISLAMABAD: The government will not fully disclose the assets of civil servants due to security concerns and will instead publish selected information by December this year to meet requirem­ents of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal told the National Assembly Stan­ding Committee on Finance and Revenue on Thursday. However, parliamentarians questioned why full details would not be made public when politicians, including the president and prime minister, were required to disclose their assets. They questioned why public servants should be treated differently when parliamentarians and politicians were required to make full asset declarations. Mr Bosal did not directly respond to the objection but said a lot of technical work had been undertaken by the Establishment Division and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). Under the mechanism, the FBR would assess the data and report its findings to the Establishment Division, which would have the power to initiate disciplinary action in case of any discrepancy. The fi­­nance secretary said civil servants’ asse­­ts would be declared under prescribed gui­delines but would not be published in full. The government has already moved to digitise declarations of income and assets of all federal civil servants in BS-17 and above, replacing the existing manual submission process with a dedicated FBR online portal. The declarations will undergo risk-based verification, while selected non-sensitive information will be made public. Soon afterwards, the Ministry of Fin­a­nce published on its website an office me­­morandum issued by the Establishment Division last week regarding the “digitisation of declaration of assets under Section 15-A of the Civil Servants Act, 1973”. According to the memorandum, the Establishment Division, in collaboration with the FBR, has launched a digitised system for the submission, verification and publication of declarations of income and assets under Section 15-A of the Civil Servants Act, 1973, and Rule 12 of the Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules, 2026. All officers in BS-17 and above are required to submit their declarations of income and assets for financial year 2025-26 through the dedicated FBR portal instead of the existing manual process. The deadline for digital filing has been set at Oct 30, 2026, in accordance with Rule 12(6) of the Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules, 2026. Under the new mechanism, officers will first have to provide their name, designation, personal active email address, mobile number and CNIC to their respective cadre administrator for creation of an account on the FBR portal. The cadre administrator will forward the officers’ details to the FBR, which will notify them about account creation through email, SMS or other prescribed means. Officers will then activate their accounts using their CNIC and a one-time password to set their own password. Once logged in, officers will find a “Declaration” option on the FBR portal dashboard. By selecting this option, they will be required to enter the requisite information through subsequent screens, with the details specified in Annex-I of the Establishment Division’s memorandum. The information submitted by officers will subsequently be subjected to risk-based verification checks by the FBR, which will communicate the results to the relevant cadre administrator. Establishment Division said selected non-sensitive sections of the declarations would be published on the FBR website for information of the general public. The declarations must be filed within the prescribed deadline, while any rectification of errors on the portal will be permissible up to Nov 30, 2026, subject to approval or authorisation of the cadre administrator concerned. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.description: El Ejecutivo se ha puesto de nuevo manos a la obra con el texto del real decreto ley de vivienda que circuló en julio y que no logró los apoyos suficientes en las conversaciones preliminares para presentarlo en el Congreso. El borrador, de 69 páginas, incide en puntos muy diversos que afectan al mercado inmobiliario: desde la ley de arrendamientos urbanos a la ley del suelo, pasando por la de enjuiciamiento civil, la de haciendas locales y todo tipo de tributos que pueden penalizar o incentivar los arrendamientos. La diferente aproximación, casi filosófica, de los grupos políticos sobre los derechos y deberes alrededor de la propiedad de la vivienda, hace que algunas de sus visiones sean irreconciliables a la hora de conseguir una mayoría parlamentaria. Los puntos más candentes son precisamente la limitación a los desahucios —que algunos temen abra la puerta a la okupación—, la congelación de los alquileres, el uso de la fiscalidad o la flexibilidad en las licencias para acelerar la construcción de viviendas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La ola de indignación por el caso Maricarmen presiona a Junts antes de una votación clave por los desahucios
items.description: El desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal , jubilada de 87 años que ha sido expulsada de un piso del barrio madrileño del Retiro donde llevaba viviendo los últimos 70 años, ha disparado la indignación ciudadana y ha puesto la lupa en como evoluciona la gestión política del caso . Si la vivienda es un motivo de inquietud principal para las personas que residen en España, una encuesta del CIS cifra en un 41% el porcentaje de ciudadanos que dicen estar preocupados por las complicaciones que conlleva encontrar un lugar donde vivir y poder pagarlo, el caso de la anciana madrileña no hace más que multiplicar la crispación. En medio del fuego, Junts per Catalunya es el destinatario de un flujo de presión de alta densidad que busca respuestas antes de que, el próximo martes, el Gobierno trate de desbloquer el real decreto ley de vivienda . Seguir leyendo

items.title: La impotencia dicta sentencia: “Descuartizó a mi madre y tuvimos que pactar para que no saliera de la cárcel”
items.description: La abogada había citado a Ferran Montón junto a sus hijas Thais y Thania a una videollamada urgente para revelarles la peor de las noticias: “Van a soltar al asesino”. Cuando las hermanas escucharon estas palabras, sintieron que el suelo desaparecía bajo sus pies. No entendían cómo la justicia iba a dejar libre al hombre que a finales de 2021 ahogó, quemó y descuartizó a su madre, Carmen Ortiz, de 57 años. Su letrada, Nuria Milà, les explicó la crudeza de la ley: una persona no puede pasar más de cuatro años en prisión preventiva y el procedimiento judicial para aclarar el asesinato se había dilatado tanto que ese límite estaba a escasas semanas de cumplirse. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La deuda de la justicia con Dolores Vázquez: 25 años sin reparar los 519 días de cárcel de una inocente
items.description: Pocos días antes de jubilarse, el juez Fernando González Zubieta citó en su despacho de la Audiencia de Málaga al penalista Pedro Apalategui. “Por favor, dile a Dolores Vázquez que le tengo cariño y deseo que sea feliz”. No solo hay cordialidad en ese mensaje. Ahí adentro se puede intuir un pesar rocoso cimentado durante años, los que habían pasado desde que el magistrado condenó en 2001 a Dolores Vázquez a 15 años y un día de prisión por un asesinato que no cometió. “Que me dijera aquello le honra. Le vi dolido. Fue el único”, afirma Apalategui en su casa de Málaga, a pocas semanas de que se cumplan los 25 años de un juicio que le marcó la vida. Nadie más de los que levantaron aquella pira en la que ardió Dolores Vázquez le mostró arrepentimiento . La vista había sido un espectáculo, concluida con el público aplaudiendo el veredicto como en un teatro mientras Apalategui cubría con su toga a la acusada para impedir que las cámaras grabaran para la eternidad su desmoronamiento. Vázquez se había sentido protegida tras su inocencia e insistió en ella en su alegato final: “Busquen a los culpables, que están ahí fuera. Nunca han tenido nada contra mí y no lo tendrán porque soy inocente”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘La bola negra’: estética e hipersensible
items.description: Pocas veces he constatado un grado tan alto de expectación no ya entre la cinefilia, sino también en gente de la calle que quiere saber mi opinión sobre una película titulada La bola negra . Viene avalada por premios lujosos en festivales, en la tantas veces falsa suposición de que esos galardones han sido bendecidos por la infalible gracia de Dios, y por una espectacular campaña de marketing cultural y apoteosis de lo woke . Y uno es proclive a las manías y a los prejuicios. Pero estoy dispuesto a creerme la excelencia cinematográfica de Javier Ambrossi y de Javier Calvo (el público y los profesionales deberían prescindir de ese colegueo tan moderno de identificarlos todo el rato como Los Javis), después de haber quedado fascinado con su talento visual y expresivo, con su capacidad para inventarse un universo tan siniestro como mágico, con su poder para transmitir una atmósfera entre misteriosa y lírica como hicieron en su admirable serie La Mesías . Seguir leyendo La bola negra Dirección: Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo. Intérpretes: Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Lola Dueñas, Penélope Cruz, Glenn Close. Género: drama. España, Francia, 2026. Duración: 159 minutos. Estreno: 25 de septiembre.

items.title: ‘La bola negra’... y las otras pocas veces en que Federico García Lorca se ha asomado a las pantallas
items.description: Durante la escritura del guion, incluso acercándose el rodaje, Javier Ambrossi y Javier Calvo dudaron si Federico García Lorca tenía que aparecer o no en La bola negra. Sí sabían quién tenía que encarnarlo: el dramaturgo malagueño Alberto Cortés. Así que fueron ellos quienes le llamaron y le pidieron que hiciera una prueba para “un personaje”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Victoria Luengo: “Me da miedo que la gente se canse de verme. Yo acabo harta de mi sobrexposición”
items.description: Victoria Luengo (Palma, 36 años) está felizmente cansada. Y defiende que se encuentra tanto en momento gozoso, en el que disfruta y sabe que no tiene derecho a la queja, como de necesidad de parar. Más de sobreexposición que de trabajos, porque, como espeta: “A ver, si llegan estas películas, ¿a cuál digo que no?”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ansiedad, gastos y resaca: “Los cumpleaños se han convertido en auténticos festejos medievales”
items.description: Has sido añadido al grupo . El mensaje, al aparecer en nuestra pantalla principal de WhatsApp, ya inspira una mezcla de hastío y ansiedad. Y puede resultar aún más desgastante cuando el grupo en cuestión es para organizar un cumpleaños. Fiesta de . Al aluvión de mensajes se añade la posibilidad de que, pocos minutos después, aparezca otro grupo para ponerse de acuerdo sobre qué regalarle al cumpleañero. Regalo de . “Los grupos de WhatsApp son otro universo”, explica Sandra, abogada. “Estoy permanentemente metida en 1.000 grupos llamados REGALO DE X , cada uno de ellos con su encuesta, brainstorming , Bizums, el drama de la persona que no contesta y retrasa las gestiones y la que propone un regalo como si estuviéramos comprando entre todos un apartamento. Me encanta regalar y celebrar a mis amigos, pero cuando encadenas varios cumpleaños, entre regalos, cenas, taxis, viajes y demás, termina siendo casi una partida fija del presupuesto mensual”, asegura con resignación. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Intento de suicidio
items.description: “Durante mucho tiempo me acosté temprano”. Tales son las primeras palabras del primer tomo de A la busca del tiempo perdido , la obra monumental de Proust, en las que uno permanece apresado debido a la discrepancia feroz entre su sencillez aparente y su complejidad real. La frase está atiborrada de tiempo. “Durante” se refiere a un período. “Mucho” lo dilata. “Tiempo” lo nombra. “Temprano” nos remite a la hora. Hasta “acosté” está conjugado en pasado. Solo parece quedar fuera “me”, un pronombre de dos letras prendido en medio de ese artefacto temporal. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cantos de sirena mecánicos
items.description: El mundillo literario francés está en llamas. A principios de esta semana, la novela C’était ça ou mourir , del quebequés de origen haitiano Thélyson Orélien, recibe el Premio de Novela Fnac. La crítica afirma que se trata de una novela extraordinaria, con un lenguaje único; un relato desgarrador, como son o parece que tienen que ser los relatos ahora, que mezcla las vivencias del autor con una pluma fina, valiente, poco habitual, ¡insólita! Todo hace pensar que puede ganar incluso el Goncourt. Un único problema: en las redes sociales, una cuenta anónima acusa al libro de estar redactado con inteligencia artificial (IA). La cuenta somete cada capítulo a un detector, Pangram, cuya tasa de falsos positivos se estima en uno de cada 24.000. Los resultados son inequívocos: los 35 capítulos del libro están escritos por la IA. El autor lo niega, la editorial lo niega, todos hablan de falsos positivos; autoras de mérito incontestable como Virginie Despentes denuncian una caza de brujas aupada por la extrema derecha contra una voz poscolonial y racializada. Las mismas pruebas, aplicadas a otras novelas de autores haitianos, las dan por humanas. Ojo a la ironía: Grasset, que denuncia el racismo de sus críticos, es la editorial que abandonaron más de 100 autores tras el despido de su director, atribuido al magnate conservador Vincent Bolloré. La pregunta de fondo es complicada, a la vez sencillísima: a estas alturas, ¿somos capaces de saber si un texto lo ha generado una inteligencia artificial o lo ha escrito un humano de carne y hueso? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bolaños acusa al Poder Judicial de buscar la “impunidad total” del juez Peinado
items.description: Las tensas relaciones que mantienen desde hace meses el ministro de Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes, Félix Bolaños, y el Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) se han recrudecido en las últimas semanas a cuenta del archivo por parte del Consejo de las quejas de Bolaños por la actuación del juez Juan Carlos Peinado cuando le interrogó como testigo por el contrato de Cristina Álvarez, la asesora de Begoña Gómez. Después de que el CGPJ rechazara el pasado martes el recurso del ministro contra esa decisión y diera carpetazo de forma definitiva a sus quejas , Bolaños ha recurrido ahora la negativa de la autoridad disciplinaria del Consejo a entregarle una copia íntegra del expediente de su caso. En el escrito, dirigido a la comisión permanente del CGPJ y al que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS, Bolaños acusa al Consejo de alargar la tramitación de su denuncia y resolver con “repentina urgencia” su archivo definitivo con el objetivo de favorecer la “impunidad” de Peinado, que se jubila esta semana. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El ‘caso FP’ que salpica al Gobierno de Ayuso tropieza con 30 cajas llenas de documentos sin digitalizar por la Comunidad de Madrid
items.description: La jueza del caso FP , que investiga la presunta comisión de un delito de prevaricación administrativa en obras de centros educativos públicos de la Comunidad de Madrid acometidas entre 2021 y 2023, ha ordenado digitalizar unas 30 cajas sin índice repletas de documentos de la Comunidad de Madrid que languidecían en los juzgados de Plaza de Castilla desde al menos junio ante la dificultad para consultarlas. La decisión, que debe traducirse en la creación de un CD con un índice temático que permita su consulta, refleja la complejidad de una causa que salpica al Gobierno de Isabel Díaz Ayuso por el supuesto fraccionamiento ficticio de contratos y facturas (a través de contratos menores) para otorgar a dedo una docena de obras que deberían haber salido a concurso público por su millonaria cuantía. La Abogacía General de la Comunidad de Madrid justificó el envío en papel alegando la imposibilidad de remitir ese volumen documental a través de LexNET. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mikel Oyarzabal: “Muchas veces la mejor acción es no tocar el balón”
items.description: Mikel Oyarzabal (Eibar, 29 años) se muestra tan alérgico a los focos como relajado en la conversación. No se gusta en sus respuestas, pero es claro. También amable y, sobre todo, práctico. Tiene las cosas claras. Una réplica de cómo juega. Marcó el gol del triunfo de la Eurocopa 2024 ante Inglaterra, mañana rival de España en el estreno de la Nations League (20:45), y se marchó del Mundial 2026 como el máximo goleador de la Roja (cinco dianas). Símbolo, si se quiere, del éxito de la España de Luis de la Fuente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Lili Reinhart, la actriz que busca el éxito lejos de los tópicos de Hollywood
items.description: Lili Reinhart (Cleveland, 30 años) no está interesada en ser una celebridad. Así lo ha demostrado durante su carrera cinematográfica. En el momento en el que su nombre empezó a ocupar titulares por su papel protagonista en la serie Riverdale (2017-2023), en la que interpretó a Betty Cooper, el control sobre lo que quería —y lo que no— en su vida pareció escaparse de sus manos. Al mismo tiempo que su fama iba creciendo, también tuvo que enfrentarse a sus inseguridades y a la exposición constante de una vida que, de repente, pertenecía también al público. Quizá por eso estos últimos tres años ha estado construyendo su carrera lejos del ruido mediático. Pero acaba de volver al centro de la escena. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cuando la melena cambia con el tiempo: “Los productos que prometen resultados mágicos no solo suelen ser ineficaces, sino que pueden hacer perder un tiempo valioso”
items.description: Tener o no tener buen pelo ha preocupado a humanos de todo tipo de sociedades. Escribe el egiptólogo Jean-Claude Goyon, en uno de los ensayos de 100.000 years of beauty (Gallimard), sobre qué llevaba a los egipcios de clase alta en la Antigüedad a usar pelucas: “Para lucir la apariencia más hermosa y demostrar el propio rango, tanto en la sociedad como en el templo, se requería un grado de perfección y control del cabello que solo una peluca podía garantizar”. La búsqueda de la melena impoluta no es nueva, como tampoco la preocupación por la disminución de su densidad, aunque nunca estos problemas habían generado tanta conversación como hoy. Se prevé que el mercado del cuidado capilar prácticamente duplique su tamaño en una década, según Grand View Research, mientras que las búsquedas en Google relacionadas con tratamientos para su caída d crecieron un 450% en 2025. “Es uno de los temas que más ha cambiado de las charlas en el salón”, reconoce el peluquero Gabriel Llano sobre su centro homónimo en Madrid (Velázquez 71), “antes las clientas acudían preocupadas principalmente por el color, el encrespamiento o el daño provocado por herramientas de calor. Hoy muchas llegan preguntando directamente por la densidad”. Seguir leyendo Estilismo: Paula Delgado. Peluquería: Fernando Torrent (Kasteel Artist Mangement) para Shu Uemura. Modelo: Sofietje Schutte (Ford Models). Producción: Cristina Serrano. Asistente de estilismo: Rubén Cortés. Asistente de producción: Marina Marco.

‘EA Sports FC 27′, el rey de los videojuegos de fútbol, vuelve dispuesto a derrotar incluso a Oliver y Benji
items.description: A los entrenadores de fútbol les gusta repetir que no hay partidos fáciles. Ni cuando sus estrellas millonarias afrontan a cajeros, abogados y carpinteros que juegan más por pasión que por un (segundo) sueldo. Sin embargo, el videojuego rey del balompié, EA Sports FC, lleva años ganando sin complicarse demasiado, incluso antes de saltar al campo. Por su poderío y sus virtudes, por supuesto. Aunque también por incomparecencia de contrincantes. Ni perder el nombre FIFA, tras romper su acuerdo con el gobierno del fútbol mundial , le sacó del trono que ocupa con comodidad. Su última entrega, EA Sports FC 27 , trata desde hoy de confirmar el reinado, con novedades de juego y modalidades. Pero, enfrente, empieza a tener rivales creíbles. Mbappé, Putellas, Haaland y compañía hasta deben medirse con Oliver y Benji, protagonistas del reciente Captain Tsubasa 2: World Fighters. Puede que el partido por la atención del público, al fin, se haya reabierto. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Xi concede audiencia a Trump
items.description: Desde la escalerilla misma del avión, toda la puesta en escena de la visita de Estado de Xi Jinping a Estados Unidos se ha convertido en un reto semiótico global. Cada gesto y cada palabra del presidente chino y de su anfitrión, Donald Trump, son interpretados en términos de la relación de poder entre las dos grandes superpotencias del siglo XXI. Las conclusiones no son buenas para Trump. El presidente estadounidense esperó a Xi el miércoles por la noche en la pista de aterrizaje de una base militar, en un gesto muy poco habitual de la diplomacia de Washington y que dejó claro desde el primer minuto que el líder chino no es un dirigente extranjero más, sino un actor cuyas decisiones pueden alterar la trayectoria de cualquier conflicto. Es la clase de recepción que Trump reservó también para Vladímir Putin en Alaska. EE UU tiene un presidente que profesa admiración a los hombres con poder absoluto. Resulta coherente con esa aspiración que durante la visita de Estado hubiera tres grandes medios de comunicación norteamericanos vetados en la Casa Blanca, por capricho de Trump. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Empanada gallega de atún, la receta casera con un truco que lo mejora todo
items.description: Hay tantas escuelas de empanada como familias gallegas. En Galicia la masa empleada solía ser la de pan, como cuenta Mónica Prego en su libro A carón do lume : “Antiguamente en las aldeas solo se hacían empanadas el día que se cocía el pan y se utilizaba la misma masa para todo”. En casa somos de masa fina y relleno discreto, como apunta Edu Lavandeira en su libro Pan Galego , cuya receta de masa de empanada hemos seguido. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Una semana antes de quedarse sin las pastillas de su terapia hormonal para la menopausia , a Gloria le llegó un mensaje al móvil: su medicación se había renovado automáticamente. items.title: Dystopia, Inc: Would you like your news with or without hallucinations?
items.description: THE obituaries of news agencies have been written on many occasions over the past two decades. First we were told we were slower than Twitter and that our global network of salaried journalists was redundant because every citizen was a journalist now. Who needs to pay for ethically-produced fact-checked content when information from the source is flowing directly into our phones in real time? We all remember the euphoria of the Twitter Revolution in Iran in 2009 and the Facebook follow-up Arab Spring (2010-2012). It was intoxicating to see the free flow of information on social networks from citizens on the front line. THE obituaries of news agencies have been written on many occasions over the past two decades. But we also all remember the brutal comedown. What happens when the autocrats shut down the internet or throw your citizens in jail? Who continues to document the story in Iran or Egypt or Syria for the outside world? It turned out social media algorithms were not driven by a need to search for the truth. Silicon Valley worked out it would make more money promoting anger and outrage. It also turned out bad actors could manipulate these algorithms to promote lies. Not surprisingly, untrained citizens were not equipped to help society navigate the pollution of our information ecosystem. Wind forward another decade and we are here again as we are presented with another ‘news agency killer’, the utopian future of Artificial Intelligence. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok can scan the world’s journalism output in seconds and spit out five juicy paragraphs to tell you about anything that’s going on in the world. This is the so-called AI Overview — it is causing traffic to trusted journalism sites across the globe to crash and it rarely pays for the expensively-produced professional journalism it hoovers up. And so again we are asked: why pay for your professional journalism when information is being deli­vered free in real time? Why waste money employing journalists to ga­­ther information that can be aggregated by our new chatbot friends? Part of the answer lies in the little chatbot disclaimer which says the information in your AI overview may actually be wrong. Would you like your news with or without hallucinations? Getting to the facts costs money, time, expertise and effort. When a huge glacial collapse in late August triggered devastating flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border leaving more than 1,300 people dead, AFP deployed a team of 11 journalists on the ground in remote parts of Nepal and India. Within an hour of police confirmation of the first major flooding three of our journalists based in Kathmandu were on the road. Prakash Mathema, Anup Ojha and Prabin Ranabhat are all Nepalese. They know the language, the terrain and the people. They carried expensive cameras and drone equipment. One of our photographers made a 13-hour journey by motorbike and truck to reach the main disaster zone. He was then able to use his contacts to take an aid helicopter further into the disaster zone. His stunning drone images of destroyed villages were seen across the world. In a catastrophe in remote areas of the planet, often there is no internet. It requires journalists to be on the ground, sometimes putting themselves in considerable personal danger, to bear witness to events. It also requires journalists who know the country and can turn to a reliable source network. While part of our Nepal team headed to the mountains, the rest remained in Kathmandu to sift fact from rumour as stories of dead and missing emerged. Many of the first reliable words and pictures published by the global media came from agencies such as AFP and our colleagues at Reuters and AP . Our clients use the content without hesitation because they know it has been gathered in an ethically correct way according to the transparent charters and trust principles which guide the work of all our journalists. They know that we have emp­lo­yed professional journalists to ga­­ther information and that we invest resources in training and expertise to ensure the people we send into harm’s way are well prepared. Clients pay for the product bec­ause they understand quality news-gathering is not cheap. They also understand we work to the same ethical guidelines from every dateline on the planet. It makes no difference whether the content comes from Nepal or New York or Gaza, it bears the same stamp of quality. On the other hand, making stuff up costs nothing. Side by side with real journalistic images from the Nepal disaster zone were reams of deep fake images showing artificially generated destroyed villages and bodies lined up for burial. The tools that have given us AI Overviews have also given every human on the planet the capacity to create confusing and damaging false images that clog up our news feeds and often go viral on social media. At AFP we employ over 100 journalists exclusively working to debunk and fact check this growing fake tide. Pushing back on lies and manipulation has become an essential journalistic complement to searching for the truth. Defending truth and facts costs money and requires values. The international agencies’ global networks remain an essential part of the fabric of the global information system. They should be cherished, and defended. The writer is Global News Director at Agence France Presse (AFP). This opinion piece was commissioned as part of the World News Day campaign — which falls on Sept 27 — highlighting the essential role of journalism in providing facts and clarity. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: La tarifa regulada del gas subirá más del 50% en octubre si el Gobierno no interviene
items.description: La Tarifa de Último Recurso (TUR) del gas natural, que se revisa trimestralmente, apunta a una subida superior al 50% entre el 1 de octubre y el 31 de diciembre, en pleno otoño. Este incremento resulta de la aplicación de la fórmula oficial que sirve para determinar el precio de esta tarifa regulada a la que están acogidos más de tres millones de consumidores (casi un 40% del total, que ronda los ocho millones). Aquel porcentaje va variando y el definitivo se conocerá el último día de este mes, aunque la asociación de consumidores OCU ya calculaba esta misma semana un incremento del 54% y las compañías del sector algo menos, pero, en cualquier caso, por encima del 50%. Y es que la fórmula recoge el fuerte incremento de los precios internacionales de la energía en los últimos meses, esencialmente el del brent. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Saudi air defences intercept 6 Houthi ‘ballistic missiles’
items.description: • Rebels target Yanbu, Taif, military sites in Jazan; push to seize key Taiz-Aden supply route • Riyadh lifts warnings issued for Makkah, Jeddah, Tabuk, other regions • UN rights chief ‘appalled’ as civilian toll climbs in Yemen RIYADH: Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Houthis on Thursday after issuing warnings for several regions, including the holy city of Makkah. The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government said the missiles were intercepted before reaching targets in Taif and Yanbu, a key Red Sea area important for Saudi oil exports. It was not immediately clear whether the attacks caused any damage or casualties. Saudi Civil Defence had earlier issued emergency alerts for several areas, including Makkah, Yanbu, Taif, Jeddah and Tabuk. The warnings were lifted mi­­nutes later. In recent weeks, similar ale­rts have often preceded Houthi attacks. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in posts on X that “escalations and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly”. The Houthis later claimed responsibility for attacks targeting Saudi military sites in Jazan province near the Yemeni border. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched a barrage involving ballistic missiles and drones aimed at what he described as operations rooms, command centers, weapons depots, missile launch sites and military camps. The latest attacks come as fighting has intensified inside Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces. At least 150 fighters from both sides were killed in the past 24 hours, according to an AFP tally based on sources from both factions. At least 98 government forces and soldiers were killed, while the Houthis said at least 52 of their fighters were killed in clashes. Many on both sides were also killed in clashes in the Kahboub Mountains and in areas between the Lahj and Taiz regions, as the Houthis seek to dominate the highlands overlooking Bab al-Mandab to protect newly seized territory. The Riyadh-backed government’s forces had earlier repelled overnight attacks by the Houthis on a key supply route to Yemen’s third biggest city Taiz from the southern port city of Aden where the internationally recognised administration is based, sources said. The Houthis have kept up pressure on government forces seeking to consolidate their power through a steep winding mountain pass. Known as Hejat al-Abd, the road is a lifeline for forces fighting on behalf of Yemen’s government, which has been hemmed in by the Houthis. The road is also critical for goods entering Taiz and its southern and western rural areas. It is the only route for residents seeking to travel abroad, with no commercial flights operating . Seizing parts of the Taiz-Aden road could allow the Houthis to tighten their grip around Taiz and deal another blow to the government. Meanwhile, the United Nations human rights chief expressed alarm Thursday over the growing civilian toll as the conflict worsens. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said he was “appalled” by the situation, warning that civilians were suffering the consequences of the renewed fighting. “As if the people of Yemen haven’t already endured enough misery, civilians are now bearing the brunt of this latest upsurge in fighting,” Turk said, adding that “civilians must never be targeted, and their protection must be the overriding priority”. Turk’s office said at least 125 civilians had been killed or injured in Houthi attacks since the beginning of August. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: Ghana still vulnerable to external shocks due to weak economic buffers – Prof Quartey
items.description: Economist Professor Peter Quartey has warned that Ghana remains highly vulnerable to external economic shocks because the country has limited buffers to absorb global disruptions. He said the vulnerability is particularly worrying because Ghana continues to depend heavily on imported processed fuel despite being an oil producer. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Prof Quartey said businesses could expect some temporary relief from borrowing costs following the Bank of Ghana’s decision to maintain the policy rate at 14%. He, however, cautioned that the relief depends on how global developments unfold. “Oh yes, certainly businesses should be comforted, but temporarily,” he said. “I mean, we should just touch wood, touch wood if nothing happens, if the prices come down, if what is happening in Iran between Iran and the U.S. doesn’t escalate and things get better, then why not?” “At the moment, it’s a temporary relief for businesses. We’re not expecting to see higher costs of credit, at least in the next month or two.” Prof Quartey said Ghana’s vulnerability becomes clearer when compared with countries facing the current geopolitical tensions. He said that such countries have reserves that can provide some protection during global disruptions. “For these countries that are even fighting, Iran, the U.S., and the rest, they have a buffer. They have oil reserves that they can fall on,” he said. “Basically, they have very little buffer to fall on, and therefore, anything that happens is that when they sneeze, we catch a cold.” He identified Ghana’s limited domestic fuel processing capacity as one of the major weaknesses. “And I think we are not processing enough of the oil. We are an oil producer, but we are not processing quite a good chunk of the oil,” he said. “We still continue to import processed fuel, and that is a big problem for us.” Prof Quartey also raised concerns about Ghana’s continued reliance on fossil fuels while other countries accelerate their transition to alternative energy sources. “Secondly, we’re relying too much on fuel, petrol and, you know, crude, for instance, whereas in other countries, other forms of fuel, green energy, green transition is happening rapidly,” he said. “That is not happening so much with us, and I think that makes us very vulnerable to external shocks.” He also pointed to Ghana’s dependence on gold for export earnings as another source of vulnerability. “And if you even look at our exports, for instance, at the moment, gold accounts for almost 60% or 61% of our export earnings,” he said. “That puts you in a very vulnerable situation.” “Should gold prices tumble, or should anything happen to the international market, we are likely to suffer the consequences.”

items.title: Situationer: Déjà vu at D-Chowk?
items.description: KHYBER Pakhtunkhwa is on edge again, and not just for the deteriorating security and volatility in the south, which has been bad for quite some time now. It is the provincial government’s avowed single-point agenda to secure its party’s chairman’s freedom from Adiala jail, or at the very least, get him some relief like shifting him to a private hospital in Islamabad. But days before ‘D-Day’, i.e. Sept 27, one cannot help but be struck by an overwhelming sense of déjà vu: this is November 2024 all over again, albeit with some changes to the cast. Ali Amin Gandapur, the chief minister at the time, who led the long march to D-Chowk, lost the job during his second year in office, allowing a young and relatively inexperienced Sohail Afr­idi to take up the mantle . One year into his term, the 37-year-old CM Afridi is now playing his biggest political gambit since his foray into politics as a student activist of the PTI’s student wing. There is another change to the cast. Bushra Bibi, the former first lady who led the bloody Nov 24 D-Chowk March, is now serving a jail term in Adiala jail. And so, the task of securing Imran Khan’s release has passed on to another woman — his sister, Aleema Khan. She too, though, has now been taken into custody . With the planned political onslaught on the federal capital just two days away, the clock is ticking, and worryingly, no one knows where and how this will end. No one has a clue. Not even those who have planned for this day for months. And neither do the ones who have scrambled to throw in all possible measures to defend and protect Islamabad from yet another onslaught from KP. The stakes are high and everyone with an insight knows it. The comparisons between the two guards are natural; Ali Amin was an old hack. He knew what he was getting into and would war-game it. But even he couldn’t forestall a mob that crossed over into the so-called Red Zone, precipitating violence in a way that was not foreseen. But Afridi is a relatively new campaigner, carrying the relentless pressure of the party’s D-Chowk fiasco. It seems he doesn’t know the full breadth of what he is getting into. These are uncharted waters for him and he doesn’t have the comfort of many wise counsels. Even the party’s own decision-making system is so diffused that no one is willing to publicly take responsibility for any fallout of the impending march; everyone is looking towards each other. Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas, the PTI’s current political mentors, are there to lend their support. But any decision, they have made clear, has to come from the PTI itself. Up until now, no one person knows what the whole plan is. With a crackdown on its leaders and lawmakers underway and authorities in Islamabad putting up several layers of security around the federal capital amid ominous warnings of nasty things to come, the PTI leadership can be under no illusions; this time around would be a different and dangerous gambit. There are logistical and financial issues as well. A party which had no dearth of resources finds itself struggling to raise money to mobilise its workers and pay for logistics. Adding to their woes is the unwillingness of private transporters to ferry party supporters, after having suffered huge losses to their vehicles in the Nov 2024 fiasco. So, what could be the game plan once party workers and supporters are eventually mobilised despite all the difficulties and misgivings? Stop at Swabi, just short of KP’s boundary with the Punjab on the M1 Motorway, and block the many entry points into Punjab? Stage a sit-in; but for how long? Will it be sustainable? Not just logistically but also politically, given the problems that the blockades would cause to the people, and the food and fuel shortages that these would give rise to? Or, will the PTI surge ahead, removing all the hurdles and battling police and Rangers to find an opening to enter Islamabad and bring the federal government to its knees, forcing it to accept their demands? If that is the case, then who will lead the charge? Who will take responsibility in the event of something going terribly wrong? It doesn’t take long for a seemingly well-organised ral­ly to turn into a mob; after all, even Ali Amin had not foreseen what would happen when his party workers entered the Red Zone. The risks are too high and everyone knows it — most of all the minders in Islamabad. PTI leaders now say, they are showing signs of panic by barricading their territory, placing containers and digging up roads to make them impassable. For the federal authorities, the risk of mob violence is too real to ignore. The events of Nov 2024 are still fresh in their memory and they can’t afford ano­ther violent confrontation so close to the Red Zone. Allowing the PTI to stage a sit-in anywhere near Islamabad is a big no-no for them; it was tried and tested, and it failed. The choices are limited. The PTI cannot afford a repeat of what happened in November 2024. Such an eventuality, they know, will hurt them gravely and might even cost them their government in KP. It is a suspense thriller, that’s for sure. No one kno­ws, neither in Peshawar, nor in Islamabad, how eve­nts will unfold in the days to come. Most worryingly, though, no one is talking to anyone, and no one knows who will initiate negotiations to end this deadlock. For some strange reason, in the words of a senior PTI lawmaker, they are looking to divine intervention to toss up some middle ground, or face-saving. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: IA : les femmes largement exclues d'une révolution numérique dominée par les hommes
items.description: Alors que les réflexions globales autour de l'intelligence artificielle (IA) se concentrent fréquemment sur ses dérives prospectives pour l'humanité, l'essor de ces technologies produit déjà des effets discriminatoires tangibles à l'encontre des femmes. Un nouveau rapport d'ONU Femmes, dévoilé à New York en marge du débat général de l'Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, met en lumière un fossé de genre persistant qui traverse l'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur de l'IA, de la conception logicielle aux instances de gouvernance. Le document dresse le constat d'une industrie largement masculine. À l'échelle mondiale, les femmes ne constituent que 22 % des professionnels du secteur, tandis que leur présence au sein des postes de direction chute sous la barre des 14 %. Cette sous-représentation aux sommets décisionnels confie de fait l'orientation stratégique, éthique et normative de ces technologies émergentes à une écrasante majorité d'hommes, risquant de cristalliser dans le monde numérique les biais et inégalités structurelles du monde réel. Cette fracture ne se limite pas à la production des algorithmes ; elle s'observe également dans leur adoption au quotidien. Selon l'étude Gender Snapshot 2026, les femmes présentent une probabilité inférieure de 20 % à celle des hommes quant à l'usage des outils d'IA générative, un écart susceptible de fragiliser leur employabilité face aux mutations du marché du travail. Il ressort également des analyses de l'Organisation internationale du Travail (OIT), que les métiers à forte prédominance féminine s'avèrent près de deux fois plus exposés aux risques d'automatisation et de restructuration induits par ces nouvelles technologies. Parallèlement, la montée en puissance de ces outils accentue la vulnérabilité des femmes face aux violences numériques. L'étude d'ONU Femmes souligne que près d'un quart des attaques en ligne ciblant des défenseures des droits humains, des militantes et des journalistes impliquent désormais l'usage de technologies basées sur l'IA, amplifiant la diffusion de contenus diffamatoires et la reproduction de stéréotypes sexistes. Face à ces dérives, l'agence onusienne interpelle les États, les entreprises technologiques et les acteurs du développement afin qu'ils instaurent des cadres réglementaires plus stricts. L'enjeu réside dans l'intégration effective des femmes aux processus de décision et de développement de l'IA, préalable indispensable pour éviter que ces innovations ne pérennisent, à grande échelle, la marginalisation d'une moitié de la population mondiale. The post IA : les femmes largement exclues d'une révolution numérique dominée par les hommes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Govt working on 174 IMF-sought tweaks, NA panel told
items.description: • Proposed changes to be placed before parliament for approval • IMF mission to begin its review on 28th; Kristalina praises Pakistan’s performance in meeting with PM Shehbaz • Sovereign Wealth Fund, remittances, sugar policy among areas under discussion ISLAMABAD: The government on Thursday said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was seeking about 174 amendments to various laws to improve governance in the financial sector, state-owned enterprises, foreign remittances, climate change and local currency integration as part of its two ongoing programmes worth $8.4 billion. “There are a total of 174 amendments the IMF wants to be passed,” Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal told the National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, presided over by Syed Naveed Qamar. He said the government was working on the amendments, which would be placed before parliament for approval. The statement came ahead of formal negotiations with a visiting IMF staff mission for the fourth review of the $7bn Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the Resilience Support Facility (RSF), beginning on Monday. A day earlier, IMF Mana­ging Director Kristalina Geor­gieva — who met PM Shehbaz Sharif on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly — appreciated the country’s performance under its programme and praised the government’s efforts for economic stabilisation, which she noted were yielding tangible results. Mr Bosal said changes to the Sovereign Wealth Fund (SWF) law were also part of the discussions. He said the IMF had been clearly told that the proposed amendments would be presented to parliament, but their approval remained parliament’s prerogative. The SWF, covering five maj­or blue-chip companies, incl­u­ding OGDCL and Pakistan State Oil, has been a critical debating point of discussion as the IMF wants their governance and financial reporting standards to be brought at par with those applicable to other state-owned enterprises. The SWF group was created as a prospective investment vehicle for government-owned entities from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE, but little progress has been made. Mr Bosal said the government was also holding discussions with the IMF on remittances, which were critical to Pakistan’s external stability. He said efforts were needed to address costly payment-system impediments, while the IMF had strongly opposed subsidies for facilitating remi­ttances. Such subsidies, which had previously crossed Rs120bn, have already been withdrawn. He said changes to the sugar policy were also among the benchmarks for the IMF review and that the federal government had circulated a draft policy for liberalisation. Three provinces had agreed to the policy, while one had raised reservations that needed to be addressed. Committee Chairman Nav­eed Qamar questioned the government’s strategy for power distribution companies (Dis­cos), particularly the fate of loss-making entities. “You will give away the profitable Dis­cos, but what will happen to the remaining ones?” he asked. The panel stressed that economic reforms should be underpinned by a coherent, transparent and sustainable strategy, particularly where their implementation could impose additional costs on consumers, businesses and productive sectors of the economy. Mr Qamar said fiscal consolidation should be accompanied by measures to promote investment, exports, employment and sustainable economic growth. Members emphasised that assessment of the IMF programme should not remain confined to formal compliance with prescribed benchmarks but should also determine whether reforms were translating into measurable economic and social outcomes. The committee sought clearer information on implementation timelines, outstanding commitments, effectiveness of public expenditure and the implications of various reforms for citizens, businesses and taxpayers. The finance secretary reported that approximately $4.5bn had been disbursed by the IMF and three programme reviews had been completed. He said the programmes were supporting balance-of-payments needs and macroeconomic stability while requiring reforms relating to revenue mobilisation, debt sustainability, fiscal consolidation, taxation, the energy sector, SOE governance and trade liberalisation. The committee was informed that key programme commitments included parliamentary consideration of supplementary expenditure beyond approved budgets, restrictions on new tax amnesties and preferential tax treatment, energy-sector reforms and implementation of the National Fiscal Pact with the provinces. The panel also examined the retailer tax-registration scheme, with members questioning its limited initial participation and seeking a measurable assessment of its effectiveness. The committee called for an evaluation covering the number of registrations, revenue generated, compliance outcomes and whether the scheme’s existing design required further adjustment. It stressed that the finance ministry should assess the scheme’s performance over a defined period and hold implementing authorities accountable against clearly stated objectives. Members also sought detailed data on industrial captive-power users that had shifted to the national grid and asked for clarification about the implications for gas and petroleum consumption and circular debt. They said implementation of energy-sector reforms should be assessed against actual operational, financial and economic outcomes. The committee also reviewed the governance framework for state-owned enterprises and the reporting relationship between government-owned entities, their respective line ministries and the finance division. Officials said reporting lines had been clarified and proposed amendments were aimed at strengthening boards, improving governance and enhancing investment discipline within the Sovereign Wealth Fund framework. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: Nigeria’s petrol exports surge sixfold, near N1tn

items.title: Policy rate hike ideal, but would hurt businesses amid rising fuel, utility costs – Prof Quartey
items.description: Economist Professor Peter Quartey has backed the Bank of Ghana’s decision to maintain the policy rate at 14%. He says the decision is appropriate given the inflationary threats facing the economy. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Prof Quartey pointed to rising global oil prices and uncertainty over how the situation will develop. “Well, it’s certainly a good move because if you look at the threats to our macro economy, you realise global oil prices have been going up and are likely to go up,” he said. “We’re not sure what the near end is going to look like.” He said Ghana was also facing other inflationary pressures, including increases in utility charges and fuel prices. “So, and inflationary threats are there, and you’ve seen utility increases, we’ve seen increases in fuel prices at the pump, etc.,” Prof Quartey said. He therefore described the decision to keep the rate unchanged as appropriate under the circumstances. “So it is just laudable, or it’s just ideal that you maintain the rate,” he said. However, Prof Quartey acknowledged that the global economic environment could support a higher policy rate. “It’s quite a difficult one. If you really want to look at what is happening globally, you may want to hike the rate, but that would not be ideal for businesses, would not be ideal for the cost of doing business,” he said. He said the Bank of Ghana’s approach was to monitor developments before taking its next decision. “And therefore, the bank is taking the approach of basically to watch the space a little bit and see how it comes out, and then we’ll take a decision,” he said. Prof Quartey ultimately endorsed the decision to maintain the policy rate. “But I think it’s certainly in the right direction,” he said.

items.title: ‘Washington, Tehran exploring phased way out of war’
items.description: • Reports suggest Tehran could reopen Hormuz, may drop toll demand for blockade relief; but ‘neither side wants to move first’ • Gulf states press Trump for post-midterms war strategy; 80 countries call for full restoration of Gulf shipping • UAE bars Iranian airline flights WASHINGTON: US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said. The strait , through which a fifth of the world’s oil passes, has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the war. Iran wants relief from a blockade that is strangling its economy; Washington wants free passage restored for ships on the vital oil route that Tehran has kept closed. Talks are complicated by a familiar diplomatic problem: neither side wants to move first. Two Iranian sources, two regional officials and two Western diplomats said the most workable option now on the table was a staged arrangement — Iran allowing ships through Hormuz in return for an end to the blockade and, potentially, access to frozen assets. “One way forward would be to solve the crisis in stages. The first would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz,” a senior Iranian official said on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Such a deal would require Donald Trump to accept another interim arrangement, after a previous understanding collapsed in July. The US president has suggested a fuller agreement might only be reached after November’s midterm elections. A senior European official said Iranian negotiators arrived in New York “with a very long list of demands”. The White House, for its part, has shown little urgency. “Iran is desperate for a deal, President Trump holds all the cards and will make whatever decision is best for the United States,” a White House official said, adding that “crushing sanctions” and “one of the most successful blockades in history” had left Tehran “completely broke”. Trump, the official suggested, was content to let an “inevitable Iranian collapse” continue rather than be rushed into concessions. Dennis Ross, a former US negotiator, put the chances of a deal before the midterms at roughly 30 per cent, though he noted both sides had reasons to want an agreement sooner rather than later. “The blockade is what’s really squeezing the Iranians. It’s strangling them,” he said. A pre-election deal could suit Trump too, easing Gulf tensions and helping bring down petrol prices at home. After the vote, Ross said, the president may feel freer to escalate pressure or consider military options. Tehran, meanwhile, is hedging. Even as it explores a diplomatic exit, Iran is preparing for the possibility of renewed conflict, accusing Washington of using the blockade and the threat of force as instruments of coercion. “Our fingers are on the trigger,” the senior Iranian official said. “The Americans know what they need to do but, because of their excessive demands, the chances of diplomacy resolving this are extremely low.” Regional sources said Iran was prepared to drop, or at least set aside, its demand for transit fees on shipping through Hormuz in order to prioritise ending the blockade. “Iran is not primarily focused on imposing tolls in Hormuz but on preserving its administrative control of the waterway,” the senior official said. “Iran may be willing to defer the toll issue, but they are not going to give up administrative control of the strait.” At the heart of the diplomacy in New York is a fundamental tension. Washington wants pressure to produce concessions, Tehran wants pressure removed before making them, and the Gulf states want the conflict resolved without allowing the region’s strategic waterways to become enduring bargaining chips. In a separate meeting in New York, Gulf leaders pressed Trump for clarity on his strategy beyond the midterms, including whether Washington would resume military action if Iran refused to negotiate. They made clear their rejection of any Iranian control over Hormuz, insisting freedom of navigation be restored and that the strait must not become a tool of coercion — while also urging de-escalation, reflecting Gulf states’ desire to stay out of further confrontation. “It’s still not clear what Trump’s endgame is, or what the alternative to the pressure campaign would be,” said Ebtessam al-Ketbi, president of the Emirates Policy Center in Abu Dhabi. “The Iranians, by contrast, know what they want. They’re reshaping the regional landscape through Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb with a clear objective, while Washington has yet to define its roadmap.” Alan Eyre, another former US negotiator, warned that the blockade’s pressure could backfire: rather than softening its position, he said, Tehran was more likely to escalate, believing that any sign of weakness would prove fatal to the regime. Adding to the diplomatic pressure, a coalition of 80 countries called at the UN on Thursday for the full restoration of maritime navigation in the Gulf. “We call for the full restoration of navigational rights and principles without delay,” said Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid al-Zayani, reading a joint statement to journalists. UAE suspends Iranian airline flights In a further sign of tightening pressure, the United Arab Emirates announced on Thursday that it would no longer accept flights operated by Iranian carriers, aligning itself with US sanctions targeting Iran’s aviation sector. Dubai has long been a key destination for Iranian airlines, serving multiple daily flights and a large Iranian community with close business ties to the emirate. The UAE’s General Civil Aviation Authority said the suspension was “based on the US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines preventing them from using airports around the world”. The UAE, which was hit by thousands of Iranian missiles and drones early in the war, suspended trade and financial exchanges with Iran last month. On Wednesday its central bank blocked transactions with Iran’s Bank Melli, citing breaches of money-laundering, terrorism-financing and arms-proliferation rules. One passenger told AFP an Iran Airtour flight from Tehran to Dubai was cancelled shortly before departure on Thursday, after tickets had already been issued. Washington imposed sanctions on Iran’s aviation sector in early September, giving airlines until Wednesday to comply — including by halting the refuelling of Iranian aircraft — or risk being cut off from the dollar-based financial system. Iran’s main carriers were forced to cancel international flights this week as neighbouring states adopted similar restrictions; Turkmenistan turned back a flight from Tehran to Dushanbe on Thursday, an Iranian aviation official said, because it had not authorised the airline to fly. A handful of smaller Iranian carriers continue to operate abroad, notably to Armenia and to China, which has declined to follow Washington’s sanctions. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: ECG workers hit the streets over PSP, set Sept. 29 for nationwide demo
items.description: The Senior Staff Union (SSU) and Junior Staff Union (JSU) of the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) have announced plans for a nationwide demonstration against the proposed Private Sector Participation (PSP) in the company. The unions say the peaceful demonstration will take place across all operational regions on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. This was contained in a directive signed by Christopher Apawu, National Divisional Chairman, and Lucky Larry Agboka, National Divisional Chairman of the Junior Staff Union, on Thursday. The action will form part of the unions’ ongoing resistance to the PSP arrangement and will culminate in the presentation of a petition to President John Dramani Mahama. In a directive to all divisional and branch chairpersons, the unions said the petition would be presented to regional ministers in all their operational regions for onward attention. The demonstration is scheduled to begin at 8:00am and end at 4:00pm. In Accra, workers are expected to assemble at the forecourt of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), while in Kumasi, the ECG Regional Office at the Airport Roundabout has been designated as the assembly point. Workers in other regions are expected to gather at the respective ECG regional offices. The unions said the proposed routes for the demonstrations would be communicated later. Participants are expected to return to their respective assembly points after the demonstration for a briefing before dispersing. The directive forms part of a wider course of action announced by the unions earlier this month over the PSP. According to the unions, the wearing of red armbands, which began as part of their declared action, will continue until another phase of the action is announced. The unions said committees would be constituted at both the national and regional levels to organise and coordinate the demonstrations. The Public Utility Workers Union (PUWU), which is the convener of the demonstration, will lead the exercise. The unions also said PUWU had formally notified the Inspector General of Police of its intention to organise the demonstration. They cited Section 1(2) of the Public Order Act, 1994 (Act 491), as the basis for the notification. The unions said further details on the organisation of the demonstration would be communicated through the relevant committees. The unions ended the directive with the message: “Solidarity forever.”

items.title: PTI ‘still in two minds’ over march plans to Islamabad
items.description: • Panjutha hints at possibility of postponement, links it to acceptance of party’s demands for Imran’s release, snap polls, probe into May 9 events • PTI spox says no such proposal being discussed, insists only founder can postpone march • Govt deploys Rangers in Islamabad, multiple districts of Punjab ahead of PTI protest ISLAMABAD: A PTI leader on Thursday hinted at the possibility of postponing its protest march if the federal government agreed to hold elections within six to eight months, release party chief Imran Khan and other political prisoners, and investigate May 9 and November 26 crackdowns on the opposition party. Advocate Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that the protest could be postponed if these three assurances were given by the government. There was no clarity on where such a proposal originated from, which added to confusion about the PTI’s plans for its Sept 27 protest . Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram, however, denied any such proposal was being discussed at any party forum, saying only Imran Khan could take a decision even if such a proposal was on the table. “The first and primary condition is that the public mandate be respected and for that free, fair and tran­s­parent elections must be held within six to eight months,” Mr Panj­utha said, while demanding a clear guarantee that elections would be held before the end of this financial year. All political prisoners, including Imran Khan, must be released — not through any deal or political settlement, but through the courts and due process of law, he said, adding that all cases against Imran Khan were “weak”. The third demand was for a judicial inquiry into the events of May 9 and November 26. “If these three demands are fulfilled, the march can be postponed,” he said, adding that in case these demands were ignored, the PTI would be “coming with no compromise, no retreat, and no turning back”. On the other hand, Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn the above mentioned conditions were shared with the government after the D-Chowk incident, but the government had not responded positively, so the conditions were then withdrawn on the order of Imran Khan. “We have not received any concrete offer from the government side, so the long march will be held come what may. Even if we get an offer, we will demand to arrange a meeting with Imran Khan, as only he can postpone it,” he added. Sheikh Waqas said the PTI cannot afford to announce postponement of march, especially when its ministers were being abducted. In a meeting held at the opposition chamber in the Senate, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and former senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar met Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and discussed preparations for the planned long march. According to a statement issued by the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayeen-i-Paki­stan (TTAP), the participants held a detailed discussion on the prevailing situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and growing challenges to provincial autonomy. The meeting also focused on the Sept 27 march, preparations for the event and the strategy to be adopted in the coming days. Rangers deployed Separately, the federal government approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5. “Pursuant to the request made by the chief commissioner, Islamabad Capital Territory … and Home Department, government of Punjab …, the federal government is pleased to authorise deployment of sufficient strength of troops of Pakistan Rangers (Punjab) in ICT and different districts of Punjab province,” an interior ministry notification read. The deployment has been aut­h­orised under Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordin­ance, 1959, and Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, to perform functions specified under the laws, as authorised by the Islamabad chief commissioner or the provincial government. “The deployed troops may respond appropriately in self-defence to any threats or violent activities encountered in the course of their duties as per rules/regulations in vogue,” the notification stated. The Punjab government also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jam­med on Sept 27. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.title: SC rejects DHA plea for income tax exemption
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court has dismissed four civil appeals filed by the Defence Housing Authority (DHA), Islamabad, against the denial of income tax exemption under Section 49 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, ruling that DHA is not a “local authority” for the purpose. A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Yahya Afridi and comprising Justice Naeem Akhter Afghan and Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui upheld the Islamabad High Court’s Jan 14, 2019, judgement, which had answered the tax references against DHA. Justice Siddiqui authored the judgement. The appeals arose from tax references filed in 2012. DHA had filed returns for tax years 2005 to 2008, claiming exemption under Section 49(2) on the ground that it was a local authority. The returns were treated as assessment orders under Section 120. Later, the Commissioner (Audit-II), LTU Islamabad, amended the assessments for 2005 to 2007, while the Additional Commissioner (Audit-II) amended the assessment for 2008 under Section 122(5A), treating them as erroneous and prejudicial to revenue on the ground that DHA did not fall within the expression “local authority”. Before the Supreme Court, Syed Tanseer Tassaduq Bukhari argued that DHA was a statutory authority responsible for the development, planning, regulation and administration of its area, exercised public and local powers, and that the expression “local authority” should not be construed narrowly. The Commissioner Inland Revenue (Zone-II), LTU Islamabad, represented by ASC Rehan Seerat and AOR Tariq Aziz supported the high court judgement and argued that DHA lacked the essential legal attributes of a local authority. Justice Siddiqui observed that the question was not whether DHA performed public or municipal functions within a defined area, but whether the nature and extent of its statutory powers satisfied the legal attributes of a “local authority” under Section 49(2).The court held that DHA’s case did not go beyond showing that it operated within a defined area and performed development, planning, regulation and administrative functions. The court subsequently held that DHA was not entitled to the exemption. Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

items.description: Hong Kong’s first five-year plan marks an unprecedented milestone not only for its economic and social development, but also for how it governs itself. The plan, which drew on 16,000 public submissions – roughly 80 per cent from ordinary citizens – is a testament to the government’s commitment to long-term development, which shows an unusual convergence of public consensus and political will. For a city long accustomed to letting the market hold the reins, crafting a road map clear in aims,...
